title: Output probability with positive amplification parameter
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic machine with Boolean alphabet, let $r,t$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{dec}:\mathbb{N}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $v$ be a Boolean value. Suppose $N$ halts on $x$ for every choice word of length exactly $t$. The probability that the amplified machine outputs the one-symbol word $[v]$ after $t+r(2t+3)+1$ steps equals the probability that, for a uniformly chosen Boolean word $l$ of length $(r+1)t$, applying $\mathrm{dec}$ to the number of its $r+1$ consecutive blocks of length $t$ accepted by $N$ gives $v$.
hypotheses_covered: The original machine halts on input $x$ for every choice word of length exactly $t$
